newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican employers see real minimum wage rise in 97.
newsitem.headline: Mexican employers see real minimum wage rise in 97.

text.p: The head of Mexico's powerful Employers' Confederation (Coparmex) said that increases in the minimum wage for next year should exceed inflation.

"From Coparmex's point of view, next year we will have to agree minimum wage (increases) in excess of expected inflation," Carlos Abascal said in an interview. "If we want to reactivate the domestic market, we have to increase purchasing power."

Analysts expect labour leaders to demand minimum wage increases above 20 percent in talks between the government, business leaders and unions to renew Mexico's wage-price pact known as the Alliance for Economic Recovery.
Inflation next year is seen at 13-15 percent.

Some 43.5 percent of Mexico's 38 million-strong workforce earn from one to three times the minimum salary. Real wages plummeted as a result of Mexico's 1994-95 economic crisis, and this year they badly lagged inflation, which is expected to end the year at around 26 percent.

Abascal said wage negotiations for collective contracts that were not linked to the minimum wage should also offer workers attractive increases, but he stressed that wage rises should also include a productivity component.
